text:
Jordan W: Hey team, customer AcmeMedia reporting a sudden spike of 429s starting ~2026-03-13 09:12 UTC. They say org quota was bumped yesterday but requests still failing. They provided a sample response header showing `x-rate-limit-scope: org` even though the API key shows plenty of quota left. Can someone help triage?

Priya S: Thanks Jordan. Can you paste the exact response headers and the curl they used? Also, are they calling from a single shared IP (eg corporate NAT)?

Jordan W: Pasting verbatim from customer:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: rq_02c9b1f8
x-rate-limit-type: throttle
x-rate-limit-scope: org
x-rate-limit-limit: 1200
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 60
{"error":{"message":"Rate limit exceeded for organization","type":"rate_limit_error"}}
```

Curl they used (sanitized keys):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-01" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

Jordan W: Customer says they tried a different API key in the same project and still got 429s. They also tried from a laptop on home network (different IP) and it worked. So suspicious it's either org-level billing/burst or IP-based policing.

Anita M: Interesting — two possible paths: (1) org-level quota/billing block that masks as org-scoped 429, (2) our edge rate limiter applying per-IP throttles that are stronger for certain customer classes. Did the customer share `x-request-id` for one of the failing calls? I want the raw headers and the ingestion logs if available.

Jordan W: They sent one `x-request-id`: rq_02c9b1f8. I pulled the proxy logs snippet they attached:

```
[2026-03-13T09:12:01Z] ip=18.202.10.45 key=sk-acme-01 reqid=rq_02c9b1f8 status=429 scope=org
[2026-03-13T09:12:02Z] ip=18.202.10.45 key=sk-acme-02 reqid=rq_02c9b1f9 status=429 scope=org
[2026-03-13T09:12:03Z] ip=3.21.99.12 key=sk-acme-03 reqid=rq_02c9b200 status=200 scope=key
```

Priya S: Ok that lines up with their manual repro — same internal NAT IP (18.202.10.45) yields 429 across multiple keys, different public IP succeeds. Does this match any current IP-based emergency throttles?

Billing Bot: ALERT: Organization `acme-media` flagged for billing anomaly on 2026-03-12 22:40 UTC. Temporary org-level request suppression applied until manual review. See billing case #B-4872.

Samir K: @Anita @Priya can you confirm whether the billing suppressor sets the `x-rate-limit-scope: org` header? If yes, the behavior is expected (org-level block overrides key-level counters). If not, we have an edge-case where the IP throttle might be collapsing keys under same org into one bucket.

Anita M: Good call. In current architecture we have hierarchical token buckets: per-key, per-project, per-org and an independent IP-based short-term fast limiter. When org billing suppressor flips to "suppress", we set the response to 429 and annotate scope=org. The fast IP limiter returns scope=ip. If they're seeing `scope=org`, Billing Bot is likely the culprit. But there are still two oddities: (a) why the org suppression didn't block the different IP earlier (it should block across IPs), and (b) why customer sees success from home IP — maybe the suppressor was applied to a subset of frontends/regions.

Jordan W: Customer claims they were hitting our upstream in us-east-1 from corp NAT and home -> us-west-2. Could be region routing difference. They also said a new key created after the bump still got 429 from corp NAT.

Priya S: For immediate mitigation we've asked customer to rotate to a key created in a different project (temp key provided) and test from corp NAT. If they still get 429, ask them to try from a different public IP or VPN and report.

Samir K: I'm going to pick this up. Action items for eng:
- Check billing suppressor logs for org `acme-media` around 2026-03-12 22:40 UTC and verify which frontends enforced it.
- Inspect rate limiter config mapping for IP-based buckets to ensure NATed IPs don't aggregate erroneously across orgs.
- Correlate `x-request-id` rq_02c9b1f8 with ingress logs and the suppressor decision.
- Confirm header emitted by suppressor (should be `scope=org`).

Anita M: I'll add a quick test harness: spin up two ephemeral VMs, one in us-east-1 and one in us-west-2, both using same key and run a burst test to reproduce the behavior. Will paste results.

Jordan W: Customer has temporarily accepted rotating key and testing via VPN. PR update: asked them to confirm once they reproduce. I told them we'll follow up within 4 hours, escalating to eng if needed. :eyes:

Samir K: Quick note — if billing suppressor is intentionally partial (only applied to certain regions for safety) that's by design to avoid broad outages while billing investigates. If that's the case we should make that clearer in the header or the troubleshooting KB.

Anita M: Repro steps I'm about to run, posting results in thread.

```
# ephemeral repro script
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{remote_ip}\n" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-01" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```

Anita M: Preliminary results: from us-east-1 NAT (18.202.10.45) 95% 429 (scope=org). From us-west-2 (3.21.99.12) 100% 200. I've filed ENG-1178 and attached logs.

Priya S: Thanks. Jordan I told customer: short-term options: (1) use VPN / different public IP, (2) rotate to a key in a different project + confirm which region they hit, (3) request an emergency billing override via support for temporary lift.

Jordan W: Customer picked option (1) and verified success from VPN. They'll use that while finance sorts billing. They've asked for a post-mortem on why billing suppressor behaved regionally.

Samir K: I'll follow up in ENG-1178 with root-cause once we confirm if this was expected behavior (regional suppressor) or a bug (IP bucket collapse). Assigning to infra + billing.

SupportBot: Ticket created: SUP-9241 (escalated to eng, referenced ENG-1178, billing case B-4872).

Priya S: Closing loop with customer now. Will post summary and link to SUP-9241. :thumbsup:

Jordan W: Thanks all. If eng finds a codepath that misattributes scope header (org vs ip) please tag this thread.

Samir K: Will do. Leaving a note to add a KB entry about how billing suppressor interacts with region routing and IP-based limits.

Anita M: ETA for initial root-cause: 24 hours. Will update here.

Priya S: Marking customer follow-up scheduled at 2026-03-13 13:00 UTC.

Jordan W: ack.
